interactions.title: Malquin bargains for proof of the outside world
lines: DM: You know, when you cross again, the door behind you slams shut, and you hear a voice. Behind you, like, speaking… well, you hear it in several languages, I don’t know what language everybody speaks, but first in Elvish, “Are you real?” And then in Sylvan, you hear, “Travelers… from the outside?” And then in Common, “Who are you? What are your names? Why are you here?”
Finnan: Shit. Do we see anybody?

DM: Yeah, yeah, I mean, as you turn around, you see the guy, the person I showed you before, appeared, like, as the door slammed shut, like, as you walked forward, not on the throne, appears behind you, and starts, like… It’s almost like a startup, like… appears out of nowhere and, like, shouts, like, “Are you real?” Well, I don’t know, do any of you speak Elvish?
Finnan: There. Finnan will respond in Elvish: “We are real.”
DM: “Hold your tongue,” he says. “That is not a language of the real.” In Common.
DM: It put… he points it at Eolo. “You. Where do you fly to with those wings? There’s nowhere to fly. There’s no up or down.”
Eolo: Well, but what's up? I, down… .
Finnan: I will say in Common… “Who are you?”

DM: He disappears and reappears on the throne, and says, seeming, like, in a totally different tone of voice, like, a much more, kind of… regal and melodious. Like, this was… he was talking, like, staccato, like, harsh, like, in a much more melodious and regal kind of voice, in… also in Common. From sitting on the throne, says…
DM: “You are here… about the cracks… in the wall. In reality, I am Malquin the Vaqar, ruler of this place. What do you know?”

Finnan: The cracks… well, they’re not just… in your dimension. They are… rips between multiple planes. They weren't just your problem. But you seem to have cultivated a very, robust culture of… stasis and fear here, so it is difficult to get any useful information about what has happened on this side. So we've come to you. If you want this solved, you'll have to tell us something.
DM: “Solved. Closed? Solved means closed, yes? Healed? Erased?”
Finnan: I mean, the alternative is to be consumed by a giant storm of lightning… swirling rainbow metal ice. So… Yes?

DM: He disappears. And appears standing, like, inches from Finnan. “Consumed! Consumed! Consumed? Being consumed by metal ice? I would consume you first. Why dare you say such things like this? Who are you to be speaking of being consumed? Nothing can consume me, I am everything.”
Finnan: That's wonderful to hear. Please then tell us how to stop the cracks. You must be the cracks if you are everything, no?
DM: “Everything outside is fake. It’s not real on the outside. So I… so I’ve been told. So… so the whispers say.”
DM: “There’s nothing beyond the edge. So the cracks must not be real either. It is a trick. A trick of… of me? Am I tricking me? That would not be… that would be cruel.”
Finnan: So why do you guard them? Why are they guarded if they are not real?
DM: Duh. My people will vanish into nothing if they go through. It will eat them, consume them, destroy them.
Justas: Where were you before you were here?
DM: “Here? I am… I’ve always been here. There’s nowhere else.”

DM: He vanishes and appears back on the throne. “I think… what?” He says, again, totally different tone of voice, “How… I would gladly… aid… your attempt to… cleanse these from the world, but I know not what you need.”
Finnan: Some volunteers. People we select to help us on this mission. Surely you can spare a few to save the rest.
DM: “Is it… how do I know you really came… from the outside?”
Justas: Unshoulders his knapsack and pulls out the severed head of the creature.

DM: He vanishes from the throne, and appears standing next to… standing, like… next, like, very, very close to Justas, and grabs… grabs the, the… to… creature’s head from you, and, like, holds it up, sort of looking at it, like, and says, “My… my other, my… my curse, my… are you… you cannot be.”
DM: And he sort of starts grabbing at the… at the base, like, trying to feel, like, is it connected to something? Like, you cannot be separated. You must come back to us.” And he sort of…
DM: Takes it, and is, like, sort of staring, like, he's almost locked, like, he's… he seems like, like… lost, like, “You must… you must be…” And then he sort of… he… he…

DM: He drops it and appears back at the throne. Seeming a little bit uncertain that, like, he hasn't… seem to be acknowledging that there’s these weird changes coming over him. “You must understand it has been… some time since we have any… had any… news from the outside. I don’t… rightly remember… what it… is.”
Finnan: When was the last time you had news?
Finnan: Why don't you come with us?
DM: “I… could… what if it is… I could not.”
DM: “The whispers say I would end. How do I know they are not correct? Ending is the worst of all fates. I could not have that.”

Justas: Could I… I wonder if I could roll an insight check. I'm… I am trying to discern whether he is under the influence of some magical or other effect external, or whether he has basically just gone mad from being you know, locked in this micro-realm for a thousand years by himself.

DM: It… it doesn't… it doesn't… seem like… like, you don’t get the sense that his… there’s a consistency, in a way. Like, there is this thread of consistency… in his speech patterns, although they are… different? Like, it's not, you know, they're a different tonality and stuff like that, but you don't… it doesn't seem like he's, like, possessed or something like that.
DM: Like… But you’re casting Detect Thoughts?
Finnan: “Of course it’s real, have you seen such creatures in here? Where do you think we came from? We’re not figments of your imagination.” I’ll hold out my hand. “Grab my hand.”
DM: And… You know, I looked up and down Finnan, like…
Finnan: You ever seen a person who looks like this before?
DM: “You seem not… unfamiliar, although I cannot say from where.”
Finnan: From before you came to this world.
Ekko: Yeah, I'll… just as a quick note, Mike, I'm also going to sense the presence of thoughts within 30 feet of myself.
DM: There's nobody else within 30 feet.
Ekko: Thinking, other than… other than us.
DM: Other than the five of you and… than him. Okay.
DM: “Now, of course,” he says, “the mind plays tricks. Of course you would seem familiar if you were not real. Proof. Proof is what is needed, you see… to solve these dilemmas. Perhaps…”
Finnan: And what… What would convince you?
DM: “Perhaps evidence it was… safe to leave. But what would that look like? Perhaps… but… but it seems, I think,” he says… “that those who go through these cracks have vanished forever.”
Finnan: I mean, we'll go through the crack.
Ekko: We'll definitely go through the crack.

Finnan: You want proof? Send us! Maybe with a few… a few other volunteers. Round up the people you don't like, the ones that you can afford to lose. Let's go through. If we survive, we'll come back and tell you. If we… if we die, then of course we won't come back. What difference does it make to you?
DM: “Hmm, you will bring… evidence… that must be… thing… a thing I give you. Hmm. It’s something I must ponder on.”((Private message logistics))

DM: I guess you could just bounce… I guess that's faster, like, why make this difficult, right? He is… He is… his topmost thought here is, like, honestly trying to think of something that he could send through… that would… that if you brought something… either something that you could bring from… from the world, or something that you could… something you could send through, and then that you would bring back… that would make him believe that the outside world is actually real. Something… “Something I could not have invented,” he says.

DM: He then… he then vanishes for a minute. He then… he appears… standing by the door, again, like, disappears and appears standing by the door. “You would steal from me, you would steal…” You can see he's, like, like, glittering sword sort of… sort of appears in his hand. “You would… you would steal my very soul? You dare offer such… offense, such terror, such horror, such end this? How dare you steal my very essence like this?”

DM: “I will see you sent away, back to the depths where you have murdered, to be murdered yourself.” He says… and then he, in the middle of his word, he vanishes again and appears back on the throne. “A thing from the outside world that I could not imagine. What could that be?”
Justas: Justas sighs and begins putting the head of the beast back into his backpack again and shouldering it.
DM: I… he says, “I remember… moonlight.”
DM: “I remember… the stars? There are no stars here. How do I remember such things?”
Finnan: Because you weren't born here.
Jrain: And therefore, you could leave… safely.
DM: But… He… he… he… he vanishes for a minute, and again, appears standing on the far side of the room… like, not by the door, but behind the throne, like, in the far corner.
DM: And he draws this glittering sword again, and, like, glittering sword of ice, and, like, stabs it into the floor, and he just screams, “You will not.” And then he disappears again.
DM: And it appears back on the throne. “Take…” And you sort of… “Take…” He… he…

DM: Takes a… takes a, like, a… a piece of, like, he's wearing a lot of, like, this, like, there's, like, these icy, like… ropes, like, around his neck. He takes, like, a… basically a necklace… and… and tosses it to you.

DM: He tosses it towards one of, like, whoever is standing, like, Finnan, I guess. “Take this… and… bring it to the night on the other side… and return it to me. That will… but you must… you must promise.”
DM: “The bargain is thus: you’ve returned this to me, having shown it to the night. And… if you do not, my…”

DM: What does he say? “You must return it to me, I will let you go. I will let… I will let you go. And you will take this, and you will show it to the night, and you will return it to me. If you do not, I will… I will curse you… as…”

DM: I don’t know, he probably says something more eloquent, I didn’t prepare what he would say, but, “I will curse you as my people do. You will not know, you know, the cold will follow you everywhere you go. And the ice will haunt you.” And he sort of looks… he glances over to where the sword is now stuck in the ice. The…
DM: That’s, that… glittering… He sort of glances and says, “My vengeance shall follow you. Will you accept this? Can you return with this?”
Finnan: I have no idea. We came through once, but we had to fight your beast. I believe we can return. But what if your beast kills us?
DM: “Then my beast will bring you my possession… will bring me my possession, it is not my problem.”
Finnan: It's kind of your problem.

DM: The… he disappears and appears next to Finnan and says, “I will enjoy it.” In his, in his, like, other sort of gravelly, different voice, “It will be delicious… when you are eaten. All should have been eaten. All of you. Fresh souls for the cycle. Yes, yes. It will be delicious.” He disappears and appears back on the throne again.
Finnan: I'm sorry. You seem to be confused about the nature of bargains. What exactly are we getting out of this?
DM: “You may leave. Is that not what you want?”
Finnan: That wasn't what we discussed.
DM: He looks confused for a minute.

Finnan: We're trying to solve this interplanar dilemma, not flee this realm. You seem uninterested in preventing the collapse of your realm to some… unknown planar forces that have already ripped a hole in it. I mean, that's fine, I guess, if you care so little about the nature… about the existence of your domain.
Finnan: But you are asking us to make a bargain to… prove the outside is real? And come back, and for what? I think your aid.
DM: “My aid in solving this problem.”
Finnan: So, if we bring back proof the outside is real to you, you will also commit… to a bargain… yes?

Finnan: I won’t make a one-sided deal. You will commit to… helping… allowing us and your people to solve this problem as they wish… without interference from you, and with as much aid as you can provide.
DM: “Allowing… I cannot allow my… people to needlessly risk themselves. Although I suppose if the outside is… truly safe…”
DM: The foremost thought you detected when he was, like, when he jumped and was… was threatening Finnan was saying, “You’ll be delicious,” but it was basically panic at no longer existing.

DM: Like, but, like, but, like, in the sense of, like, being… [garbled]? Cured is the wrong word, but, like, panic that, like, there’s this just this overriding sense of panic. I guess you don’t really know what. Like, just this sense of panic and this sense of fear, like, “What is happening to me? This doesn’t make it… this is, like, terrible.” Like, “I’m losing…” Like, this sense of, like, no… like, the thoughts were totally jumbled, right? Like, the sense of lack of control and, like… So, okay, so… And… and a sense of… of, like, growing anger, too.

DM: Anger… anger at… discussions… and talking.
DM: He says, “I would not… wish…” He sort of pauses for a minute. “I would not wish to…” He says again, “impede… those who… there is much danger. It is not…”

DM: “But if you can prove, if you… if you bring news of safety elsewhere… I would not wish to impede those who… I would not wish to impede those who to… wish… to take advantage of it. It is… so, yes, I can… I could accept that bargain.”

DM: “Proof of… the real… if you return, when you return with proof that the outside world is real… I could… help you… to close this… these cracks and… and… as you see fit, with what aid I can give. It has been a… endless… yes.”
DM: He stops for a minute. “I will, if you accept, tell…” He sort of closed his eyes for a minute. “Tell… my guardian to let you pass.”

DM: He… he, as… as you're telepathically bouncing, although I guess that doesn't take very long, he disappears from the throne, and it appears… by the door, and, like, sort of… stands, like, he, he, he, he sort of throws out his arms, and like… like, wide, and the sword comes flying to him. “Insects like you… you shall not…” “No, no, no,” he says to him, he says, he turns and says, “No, no, they are not. They are not here.” And then he turns his head like this and says, “Yes, they are. They are destroying us. They will.” “No, they are not here,” he says. DM: Well, he's standing in front of the door, although you could just try and walk past him.

DM: He sort of turns to… he turns again and says, “The outside… do not… do not,” he says. “The night is not real. The night, I create the night. It haunts us. It is not real.” “This is not… it will not,” and he shouts, he sort of turns to himself again, and, like… again, having this argument. As you’re coming closer, it’s getting louder.
DM: And he appears back… all of a sudden, he appears back on the throne. And he says, “You best hurry,” very distinctly.
